identity.public_title: Danse - a room that never repeats

copy.eyebrow: A living photographic work begun in 2017
copy.logline: A room reconstructed from one afternoon of photographs becomes a seeded, unbounded choreography that can be revisited but never rewound.
copy.concept: In June 2017, a locked camera watched a dancer move through a South Florida apartment. The tracked corpus contains 161 registered raw photographs from that session and one unregistered archival composite made afterward. Danse treats those records as spatial material: fragments from different instants can occupy depth while a single projector model keeps the room continuous. The work is not one fixed film. Each visit enters a deterministic river whose exact state can be cited by seed and time.
copy.installation_concept: The installation returns photographic fragments to physical space. Projected planes or scrim surfaces carry views from the same camera position, allowing a flat composite to open into a room as viewpoint, depth, and visitor input diverge. Venue geometry, projection, sound, recovery, and safety remain proposals until issue 14 supplies validated evidence.
copy.technical_summary: The visual engine is a pure function of a 32-bit seed and absolute river time. It can seek directly to any state without replaying earlier frames. The selected ScreenDance design follows two Delibes movements at native tempo, but score, choreography, rendered-audio, toolchain, final-cut, room-synchronization, recovery, and capture claims remain gated by exact receipts.

accessibility.alt_text: Translucent photographic fragments of a dancer and an apartment overlap in a continuous room, moving between a flat collage and suspended planes in depth.
accessibility.canvas_description: A generative WebGL composition draws from 161 registered raw photographs and one archival composite, moving between readable poses, a flat collage, and suspended fragments in one room. The same seed and time reproduce the same arrangement.
accessibility.motion_note: The live artwork contains continuous drift, changes in depth, and camera divergence. The selected capture requires phrase-length pose holds, bar-length dissolves, and no instantaneous global reseed before the final black; those behaviors remain gated by score and choreography receipts.
accessibility.audio_note: The selected ScreenDance design uses two Delibes movements rendered from an adapted MIDI and declared soundfont; exact audio, loudness, license, and captionable-event claims remain pending until their receipts and artistic approval exist.
accessibility.reduced_motion: The live root honors the device reduced-motion preference by holding a reproducible frame. The project page uses no essential animation.
accessibility.silent_fallback: The visual work and all navigation remain intelligible with audio unavailable. Final release media must document any meaning otherwise conveyed only by sound.

press.synopsis_short: In 2017 a dancer moved through a Florida apartment while the camera stood still. Danse draws on 161 registered photographs and one archival composite, returning readable poses and translucent fragments to a shared room whose exact state can be cited by seed and time.
press.synopsis_long: On 20 June 2017, a locked camera recorded a dancer moving through a one-bedroom apartment in South Florida. The tracked corpus contains 161 registered raw photographs and one unregistered archival composite made afterward. A pure seeded engine reconstructs the flat work, opens its fragments into depth, and lets each visitor enter a river with a durable identity. For the ScreenDance capture, two selected Delibes movements provide a native musical clock for whole-pose holds, bar-length dissolves, repetition, stillness, and controlled development. The score-driven film, spatial sound, and physical installation remain separately evidence-gated forms of the shared engine.
press.artist_bio: Anthony J. Padavano is a photographer and programmer working between South Florida and New York. His work treats a photograph as a record of where a camera stood and software as part of the photographic object. Final identity and biography wording require the artist's approval before publication.
press.artist_statement: The original collage was cut by feeling. The generative work asks what its sources become when they are treated as views through one camera instead of flat pieces of paper. The current solve draws on 76 registered raw photographs and the archival composite itself; that self-reference is disclosed, while new cuts use only registered camera sources. The selected score-led capture gives whole poses and dissolves musical time, but its release statement remains subject to artistic and rights approval.

seed_sharing.note: A seed names a river; seed plus time cites one reproducible instant. Public sharing remains owner-initiated and never runs as a build side effect.
